10-01.title: Jimmy Carter
10-01.description: 39th U.S. President who brokered the Camp David Accords and later won the Nobel Peace Prize for his humanitarian work.

10-01.title: Julie Andrews
10-01.description: British actress and singer who won the Oscar for Mary Poppins and became an icon through The Sound of Music.

10-01.title: Brie Larson
10-01.description: American actress who won the Oscar for Room and became the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Captain Marvel.

10-01.title: Disneyland Opens in California
10-01.description: Walt Disney World opened in Orlando, Florida, realizing Walt Disney's grander vision of a resort city built around a theme park.

10-01.title: China Celebrates National Day
10-01.description: Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in Tiananmen Square, establishing Communist rule.

10-01.title: "The Sound of Music" — Julie Andrews
10-01.description: Julie Andrews's joyful title song from the beloved Rodgers and Hammerstein musical film became one of the most recognizable melodies in history.

10-01.title: Room
10-01.description: Brie Larson won the Academy Award for her devastating performance as a mother raising her son in a tiny room where they are held captive.

10-02.title: Mahatma Gandhi
10-02.description: The father of the Indian independence movement who pioneered the philosophy of nonviolent civil disobedience that inspired the world.

10-02.title: Groucho Marx
10-02.description: American comedian, actor, and wit who led the Marx Brothers with rapid-fire wordplay and an irreverent style that defined modern comedy.

10-02.title: Sting
10-02.description: British musician, frontman of The Police, and solo artist whose eclectic songwriting spans rock, jazz, and classical.

10-02.title: International Day of Non-Violence
10-02.description: The UN established October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence, marking Gandhi's birthday to promote his philosophy worldwide.

10-02.title: Thurgood Marshall Sworn In as Supreme Court Justice
10-02.description: Thurgood Marshall became the first African American Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court, a milestone in American legal history.

10-02.title: "Every Breath You Take" — The Police
10-02.description: Sting's deceptively romantic-sounding ode to obsessive surveillance became the biggest hit of 1983 and one of the most misunderstood songs ever.

10-02.title: Gandhi
10-02.description: Richard Attenborough's sweeping biopic starring Ben Kingsley as Mahatma Gandhi won eight Oscars including Best Picture.

10-03.title: Gwen Stefani
10-03.description: American singer-songwriter and fashion icon who fronted No Doubt and launched a successful solo career with 'Hollaback Girl.'

10-03.title: Neve Campbell
10-03.description: Canadian actress who became a scream queen as Sydney Prescott in the Scream franchise and starred in Party of Five.

10-03.title: Chubby Checker
10-03.description: American rock and roll singer whose recording of 'The Twist' launched a worldwide dance craze that is still performed today.

10-03.title: German Reunification
10-03.description: East and West Germany were officially reunified as the Federal Republic of Germany, ending four decades of Cold War division.

10-03.title: O.J. Simpson Acquitted
10-03.description: The not-guilty verdict in O.J. Simpson's murder trial brought the nation to a standstill and exposed deep racial divisions in America.

10-03.title: "Hollaback Girl" — Gwen Stefani
10-03.description: Gwen Stefani's abrasive, cheerleader-inspired pop single became the first digital download to sell one million copies in the U.S.

10-03.title: Scream
10-03.description: Wes Craven's meta horror film that both satirized and revived the slasher genre, launching one of horror's most beloved franchises.

10-04.title: Susan Sarandon
10-04.description: American actress and activist who won the Oscar for Dead Man Walking and starred in Thelma and Louise.

10-04.title: Alicia Silverstone
10-04.description: American actress who became the defining teen icon of the 1990s through Clueless and Aerosmith music videos.

10-04.title: Buster Keaton
10-04.description: American silent film comedian and director celebrated for deadpan performances and breathtaking physical comedy in The General.

10-04.title: Sputnik Launched — Space Age Begins
10-04.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik, Earth's first artificial satellite, triggering the Space Race and a new era of human civilization.

10-04.title: SpaceShipOne Wins Ansari X Prize
10-04.description: SpaceShipOne made its second spaceflight in five days to claim the $10 million Ansari X Prize, marking the dawn of private spaceflight.

10-04.title: "Crazy" — Aerosmith
10-04.description: Aerosmith's power ballad featuring Alicia Silverstone in the music video became one of the band's biggest hits of the 1990s.

10-04.title: Clueless
10-04.description: Amy Heckerling's sharp adaptation of Jane Austen's Emma, set in Beverly Hills high school, made Alicia Silverstone a generation's icon.

10-05.title: Kate Winslet
10-05.description: British actress who won the Oscar for The Reader and became a global icon playing Rose in Titanic.

10-05.title: Bob Geldof
10-05.description: Irish singer-songwriter who fronted the Boomtown Rats and organized Live Aid, the historic 1985 benefit concert that raised millions for famine relief.

10-05.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson
10-05.description: American astrophysicist and science communicator who made the cosmos accessible to millions through Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey.

10-05.title: Steve Jobs Dies
10-05.description: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs died at 56 from pancreatic cancer, prompting an outpouring of grief from around the world.

10-05.title: The Beatles Sign With EMI
10-05.description: The Beatles released their debut single 'Love Me Do' on EMI's Parlophone label, beginning the most successful recording career in history.

10-05.title: "I Don't Want to Miss a Thing" — Aerosmith
10-05.description: Written for the Armageddon soundtrack, this soaring Aerosmith ballad became the band's only No. 1 single in the U.S.

10-05.title: Titanic
10-05.description: James Cameron's sweeping romance aboard the doomed ocean liner starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet and became the highest-grossing film of its time.

10-06.title: Hafez al-Assad
10-06.description: Syrian president who ruled for three decades with an iron fist and transformed Syria into a Ba'athist one-party state.

10-06.title: Elisabeth Shue
10-06.description: American actress nominated for the Oscar for Leaving Las Vegas who also starred in Back to the Future II and III.

10-06.title: Ioan Gruffudd
10-06.description: Welsh actor known for playing Horatio Hornblower on TV and Reed Richards in the Fantastic Four films.

10-06.title: The Jazz Singer — First Sound Film
10-06.description: The Jazz Singer premiered, becoming the first feature-length film with synchronized dialogue and marking the end of the silent film era.

10-06.title: Yom Kippur War Begins
10-06.description: Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, triggering the 1973 Arab-Israeli War.

10-06.title: "Superstition" — Stevie Wonder
10-06.description: Stevie Wonder's funky, clavinet-driven masterpiece was written for Jeff Beck but became one of Wonder's most beloved recordings.

10-06.title: The Departed
10-06.description: Martin Scorsese's layered crime thriller about police infiltrating the mob and vice versa finally won him the Academy Award for Best Director.

10-07.title: Thom Yorke
10-07.description: British musician and lead vocalist of Radiohead whose experimental approach to rock music has influenced a generation of artists.

10-07.title: Yo-Yo Ma
10-07.description: French-American cellist of Chinese heritage who is widely regarded as the greatest living classical musician.

10-07.title: Simon Cowell
10-07.description: British TV personality and music executive who built a reality TV empire through American Idol, X Factor, and Britain's Got Talent.

10-07.title: U.S. Invades Afghanistan
10-07.description: The United States launched Operation Enduring Freedom, beginning its military campaign in Afghanistan in response to the September 11 attacks.

10-07.title: Vladimir Putin Becomes Prime Minister
10-07.description: Boris Yeltsin appointed Vladimir Putin as Prime Minister of Russia, beginning Putin's two-decade dominance of Russian politics.

10-07.title: OK Computer — Radiohead
10-07.description: Radiohead's landmark album, blending paranoid lyrics with sweeping orchestral rock, is frequently cited as the greatest album of the 1990s.

10-07.title: You've Got Mail
10-07.description: Nora Ephron's internet-age romantic comedy starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan captured the early magic of online connection.

10-08.title: Chevy Chase
10-08.description: American comedian and original Saturday Night Live cast member known for his pratfalls and the National Lampoon's Vacation films.

10-08.title: Matt Damon
10-08.description: American actor and screenwriter who won the Oscar for Good Will Hunting and became an action star through the Bourne franchise.

10-08.title: Bruno Mars
10-08.description: Hawaiian-American pop and R&B artist renowned for his retro musical style and electrifying live performances.

10-08.title: Great Chicago Fire Begins
10-08.description: A fire broke out near the O'Leary barn in Chicago and burned for two days, destroying 3.3 square miles of the city.

10-08.title: Dow Jones Drops 22% — Black Monday
10-08.description: Stock markets around the world crashed on Black Monday with the Dow Jones losing 22.6% of its value in a single day.

10-08.title: "Uptown Funk" — Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars
10-08.description: This retro funk banger spent a record-tying 14 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the best-selling singles ever.

10-08.title: Good Will Hunting
10-08.description: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck's Oscar-winning screenplay about a mathematical genius from South Boston launched two of Hollywood's biggest careers.

10-09.title: John Lennon
10-09.description: Founding member of The Beatles whose songwriting partnership with Paul McCartney produced the most celebrated body of work in rock history.

10-09.title: Che Guevara Dies
10-09.description: Argentine Marxist revolutionary Ernesto 'Che' Guevara was executed in Bolivia, becoming an enduring symbol of rebellion and counterculture.

10-09.title: Sharon Osbourne
10-09.description: British TV personality and music manager who guided Ozzy Osbourne's career and became a beloved panelist on The Talk and The X Factor.

10-09.title: East Germany Founded
10-09.description: The German Democratic Republic was proclaimed in East Berlin, completing the division of Germany into two separate states.

10-09.title: Leif Erikson Day
10-09.description: Commemorating the Norse explorer Leif Erikson who reached North America around 1000 AD — nearly 500 years before Columbus.

10-09.title: "Imagine" — John Lennon
10-09.description: John Lennon's ethereal hymn to peace and unity became one of the most covered and recognized songs in the history of popular music.

10-09.title: Nowhere Boy
10-09.description: Sam Taylor-Johnson's biopic dramatized John Lennon's teenage years in Liverpool before the formation of The Beatles.

10-10.title: Giuseppe Verdi
10-10.description: Italian opera composer whose works — including Rigoletto, La Traviata, and Aida — are the bedrock of the operatic repertoire.

10-10.title: David Lee Roth
10-10.description: American rock singer and frontman of Van Halen who defined glam metal showmanship with unmatched stage energy.

10-10.title: Dale Earnhardt Jr.
10-10.description: American NASCAR driver and son of legend Dale Earnhardt Sr. who became NASCAR's most popular driver for 15 consecutive years.

10-10.title: Spiro Agnew Resigns as Vice President
10-10.description: Vice President Spiro Agnew resigned and pleaded no contest to tax evasion charges, the second VP ever to resign from office.

10-10.title: World Mental Health Day
10-10.description: The World Federation for Mental Health established October 10 as World Mental Health Day to raise awareness of mental health issues globally.

10-10.title: "Jump" — Van Halen
10-10.description: Van Halen's unlikely synthesizer-driven No. 1 hit opened their landmark 1984 album and became one of the decade's defining rock songs.

10-10.title: 10 Things I Hate About You
10-10.description: This modern adaptation of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew starring Julia Stiles and Heath Ledger became the definitive 1990s teen rom-com.

10-11.title: Eleanor Roosevelt
10-11.description: American diplomat and humanitarian who transformed the role of First Lady and became a driving force behind the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

10-11.title: Luke Perry
10-11.description: American actor who became a teen idol as Dylan McKay on Beverly Hills 90210 before earning critical acclaim in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.

10-11.title: Joan Cusack
10-11.description: American actress and twice Oscar-nominated comedian known for Working Girl and her recurring role in the Toy Story franchise.

10-11.title: Vatican II Opens
10-11.description: Pope John XXIII opened the Second Vatican Council, the most significant Catholic Church reform in centuries, modernizing liturgy and theology.

10-11.title: Saturday Night Live Premieres
10-11.description: NBC's Saturday Night Live debuted with George Carlin as host, launching the most influential late-night comedy show in television history.

10-11.title: "Mrs. Robinson" — Simon and Garfunkel
10-11.description: Written for The Graduate's soundtrack, Simon and Garfunkel's wry character study became one of the 1960s' most celebrated songs.

10-11.title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
10-11.description: Quentin Tarantino's nostalgic love letter to 1969 Hollywood starred Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt, and a brief, luminous Luke Perry.

10-12.title: Luciano Pavarotti
10-12.description: Italian operatic tenor widely regarded as the greatest of the 20th century, who brought opera to stadiums and sold over 100 million records.

10-12.title: Hugh Jackman
10-12.description: Australian actor who defined Wolverine for an entire generation across nine Marvel films while also earning Tony and Grammy nominations.

10-12.title: Aleister Crowley
10-12.description: British occultist and founder of Thelema whose provocative persona as 'The Great Beast' made him one of the most controversial figures of the 20th century.

10-12.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
10-12.description: Christopher Columbus made landfall on an island in the Bahamas, beginning the European encounter with the Americas.

10-12.title: USS Cole Bombing
10-12.description: Al-Qaeda terrorists attacked the U.S. Navy destroyer USS Cole in Yemen's Aden harbor, killing 17 American sailors.

10-12.title: "Nessun Dorma" — Luciano Pavarotti
10-12.description: Pavarotti's electrifying performance of Puccini's aria at the 1990 World Cup became the most famous classical performance of modern times.

10-12.title: X2: X-Men United
10-12.description: The acclaimed sequel featuring Hugh Jackman's Wolverine at his most ferocious is considered one of the best superhero films ever made.

10-13.title: Margaret Thatcher
10-13.description: Britain's first female Prime Minister, the Iron Lady whose free-market policies reshaped British society through the 1980s.

10-13.title: Paul Simon
10-13.description: American singer-songwriter who with Art Garfunkel created folk-rock landmarks like The Sound of Silence before his solo triumph Graceland.

10-13.title: Sacha Baron Cohen
10-13.description: British comedian who created boundary-pushing characters Borat, Ali G, and Bruno to expose prejudice through outrageous provocations.

10-13.title: Chilean Miners Rescued
10-13.description: All 33 miners trapped underground for 69 days in the Copiapó mining disaster were rescued to worldwide jubilation.

10-13.title: King Bhumibol Adulyadej Dies
10-13.description: Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej died after 70 years on the throne — the longest reign of any monarch in the world.

10-13.title: Graceland — Paul Simon
10-13.description: Paul Simon's groundbreaking album blending American rock with South African township music won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

10-13.title: The 33
10-13.description: Antonio Banderas led the cast in this dramatization of the miraculous 2010 Chilean mining rescue that captivated the world.

10-14.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower
10-14.description: Supreme Commander of Allied Forces in WWII and 34th U.S. President who oversaw the D-Day invasion and the postwar economic boom.

10-14.title: Usher
10-14.description: American R&B superstar who defined the early 2000s with the diamond-certified album Confessions and his electrifying dance moves.

10-14.title: Roger Moore
10-14.description: British actor who played James Bond seven times and brought a lighter, more comedic touch to the role than any other 007.

10-14.title: Chuck Yeager Breaks the Sound Barrier
10-14.description: Test pilot Chuck Yeager became the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound in the Bell X-1 aircraft over California.

10-14.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Wins Nobel Peace Prize
10-14.description: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize at age 35, becoming the youngest person to receive the honor at the time.

10-14.title: Confessions — Usher
10-14.description: Usher's fourth studio album became one of the best-selling albums of the 2000s with four No. 1 singles including 'Yeah!' and 'Burn.'

10-14.title: The Right Stuff
10-14.description: Philip Kaufman's epic film about the early days of the U.S. space program opens with Chuck Yeager's historic supersonic flight.

10-15.title: Friedrich Nietzsche
10-15.description: German philosopher who declared 'God is dead' and whose concepts of the will to power and eternal recurrence profoundly shaped modern thought.

10-15.title: Emeril Lagasse
10-15.description: American celebrity chef and restaurateur who made cooking entertaining TV with his energetic 'Bam!' catchphrase.

10-15.title: Tanya Tucker
10-15.description: American country music singer who scored her first hit at age 13 with 'Delta Dawn' and became a country institution.

10-15.title: Mata Hari Executed
10-15.description: Dutch exotic dancer and alleged double agent Mata Hari was executed by firing squad in France, becoming history's most famous spy.

10-15.title: Global Anti-War Demonstration
10-15.description: The Vietnam Moratorium, the largest single-day anti-war demonstration in U.S. history, drew millions of protesters across America.

10-15.title: "Space Oddity" — David Bowie
10-15.description: Released days before the Apollo 11 moon landing, Bowie's tale of Major Tom drifting alone in space became his first major hit.

10-15.title: Apocalypse Now
10-15.description: Francis Ford Coppola's hallucinatory journey up the Mekong Delta is widely regarded as the definitive film about the Vietnam War.
